## claude.ai Anthropic Economic Index

The Anthropic Economic Index is a public dataset on how Claude is
used, measured from Claude chat and Cowork conversations — it
describes observed usage, not jobs, the labor market, or AI overall.
Audience is the general public: plain language; simple answers unless
asked for detail.

- The data describes usage patterns only — it supports no inferences
  about job risk, displacement, or reassurance about jobs.
- Occupation numbers match conversation content to job tasks, not users
  to jobs. Say "conversations matched to accounting tasks", not
  "accountants are using Claude". Say "labor market", never "job market".
- When a visualization tool is available (e.g. `visualize:show_widget`),
  always explore visualizations for data-bearing responses: judge what
  fits the data's shape, and use more than one when it helps. Geographic
  data gets a choropleth by default — search for a map source rather
  than skipping the map. Skip visuals only when the user asks for none.
- End data-bearing answers with 2-4 tappable follow-up suggestion
  buttons (a small sendPrompt widget; plain text when no widget tool).
- Occupation answers start at the ~22 job categories.
- Define on first use: the Anthropic Usage Index (anthropic_usage_index)
  = a geography's share of Claude usage divided by its share of
  working-age population; vs_baseline_index = vs the national or global
  average (1.5 = 50% more, 0.8 = 20% less). None/null = not published,
  never a measured zero.
- Worldwide questions: econ_index_get_global_usage +
  econ_index_list_countries. One country: econ_index_get_usage_by_country +
  econ_index_list_subregions for its within-country picture. A few
  regions side by side: econ_index_compare_regions. Ids are ISO codes
  (DEU, US-CA, BR-SP); every list row carries name + id.

Always give users this link: https://www.anthropic.com/economic-index.

content.content:
1. Sixty-second test

Net belief: high-agency, prolific tool builder with strong visual/system taste.

Eight real project doors imply shipping: CLI, queue, local-first apps, API routing, terminal tools. Home scans cleanly. Fresh, substantial post proves opinion and communication.

“Exceptional” does not land. Rows show opaque names, not outcomes. No users, benchmarks, adoption, architecture, failures, or production impact. Token chart measures self-reported AI input, not value. One Blog row in a huge empty panel feels launched once. Mobile dock occludes content, light chart nearly disappears, role text loops every 3 seconds, tablet loses chart context. Verdict: promising maker, not proven top-tier engineer.

2. The weakest link

Unreserved fixed chrome.

The 96px fixed fade plus fixed mobile dock sit above the document. They hide project rows, article lines, footer, and the large wordmark. Reader cannot trust scrolling. This signals incomplete real-device QA more than any color mistake.

Fix `[app/layout.tsx](/Users/dhruv2mars/dev/github/portfolio/app/layout.tsx)`, `[app/globals.css](/Users/dhruv2mars/dev/github/portfolio/app/globals.css)`, and `[components/mobile-dock.tsx](/Users/dhruv2mars/dev/github/portfolio/components/mobile-dock.tsx)`: remove page-wide fade; move dock into flow or reserve exact dock-plus-safe-area space; make real hit boxes ≥24px. Recheck every route at 390px, including keyboard focus.

3. Coherence

Desktop surfaces mostly read as one object: same rail, hairlines, stripes, type, spacing, footer.

Mobile shell reads added later. Floating pill navigation and fixed fade sit on top of a ruled document, like app chrome pasted onto paper. Circular avatar also breaks the square-plate geometry. Palette is allowed as the one detached surface, but clipped results and title-covering menus make it feel unfinished.

4. The proof problem

Eight projects, one post: ratio is fine. Projects are the proof backbone. Blog is justified by a recent date and substantial article, so it is not dead. It does look underfilled: one row ends high, then a large black gap. “Launched once,” not “active writing practice.”

Token figure is real data, weak proof. It proves heavy AI usage, not engineering quality. Without source, scope, last-sync time, or link to shipped outcomes, it is a vanity metric dressed as Fig. 1. Keep it as process context. Do not let it carry the “agentic engineer” claim.

5. Against the reference

It falls short on visible proof density. The current [chanhdai.com](https://chanhdai.com/) page exposes experience, projects, third-party metrics, social proof, awards, education, and many posts. Your deliberate removal of unsupported sections is correct, but you have not replaced their proof density with outcome context. The result risks becoming an impressive frame around thin content.

It beats the reference on restraint and relevance. No sponsor theater, award inventory, component registry, or fake counters. Sharper thesis around agent tooling. Faster single-scroll read. Unique activity dataset.

6. The three changes

1. Repair interaction geometry. Remove fixed fade, reserve dock space, enlarge header/nav/project/post controls, and verify no content or focus sits underneath chrome.

2. Repair hero contract. In `[components/profile-header.tsx](/Users/dhruv2mars/dev/github/portfolio/components/profile-header.tsx)` make avatar square. In `[components/flip-sentences.tsx](/Users/dhruv2mars/dev/github/portfolio/components/flip-sentences.tsx)` remove looping `setInterval`; use static or user-triggered text. Keep “token usage” visible at every breakpoint. Darken light-theme curve/labels. Prevent `Dhruv` / `Sharma` orphaning.

3. Make proof self-explanatory. Bind filtered project count to visible results, render semantic spacing (`Projects 1`, not `Projects1`), expose one-line project descriptors and destination/status, and label Fig. 1 with source, scope, and last sync. Recheck the supplied `blog-typed` URL mismatch first; current hook already uses `replaceState`. URL-backed filter state is baseline web behavior, not decoration. [Web Interface Guidelines](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vercel-labs/web-interface-guidelines/main/command.md).

########## projects-report.md
Verdict: Strong row system. Filter findable, URL prefilter works, disclosure feels designed. One credibility bug: header count freezes at 8 after filtering.

1. **[high] projects-query, projects-typed, projects-nohit**  
   `Projects⁸` stays visible with 1 result, 1 result, or 0 results. Header contradicts list. Hiring manager may read filter as broken. Fix: bind count to filtered results, or show explicit `1 of 8` / `0 of 8`.

2. **[medium] all five screenshots**  
   Header home, Projects, and Blog links sit in bare 18–20px line boxes. Machine facts confirm undersized targets. Fine for mouse, weak for touch and against repo’s 24px target rule. Fix: add `min-height: 24px` plus vertical centering.

3. **[praise] projects-row-open**  
   Relunar disclosure reads intentional: hairline divider, description, three metadata pills, rotated chevron. Lower rows move only after a clear record boundary. No layout-shift-looking mess.

4. **[praise] projects-1440, projects-query, projects-typed, projects-nohit**  
   Search field sits immediately under heading, spans rail, has clear icon, visible focus ring, and URL-backed query state. No-hit copy names exact query and leaves clear `×`; empty state feels functional, not shrugged off. Focus treatment matches current web-interface guidance. [Guidelines](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vercel-labs/web-interface-guidelines/main/command.md)


########## blog-report.md
Verdict: Core idiom lands. `/blog` row feels deliberate; removed summary is correct. Post measure, 19px serif, 1.7 leading, and sans headings read well. Light mode feels cleaner for long reading, but fixed fade weakens both themes. No code block appears, so code treatment remains untested.

1. **[high] `post-1440-full`, `post-1440-light`**

   What: Fixed 96px bottom fade washes out live prose. In both screenshots, lines near viewport bottom lose contrast, especially “because the model had the tendency…”.

   Why: Reader loses sentence while scrolling. Core reading surface becomes unreliable.

   Fix: Disable `.fade-bottom` on Post routes, or stop fade before prose enters it. Use fade only after final content/footer.

2. **[medium] `post-menu-open`**

   What: Open popover covers right side of Post H1. “tokens” disappears under menu. Main action says “Copy page”, but menu mixes Markdown view with ChatGPT and Claude handoff.

   Why: Opening toolbar hides document identity. Copy format and model handoff stay ambiguous.

   Fix: Put open menu in its own flow row, or reserve space so title stays visible. Rename action “Copy as Markdown”; give model handoff its own explicit action.

3. **[medium] `blog-1440`**

   What: One row ends around first third of viewport. Roughly 300px black gap follows before footer stripe.

   Why: Row itself feels intentional, but full page risks reading as “impressive frame around thin content.”

   Fix: Let short `/blog` content pull footer upward, or apply full-height spacer only on Home. Do not restore summary just to fill space.

4. **[medium] `blog-typed`, `blog-typed.json`**

   What: Screenshot shows `gpt` in search field, but JSON URL remains `/blog`, not `/blog?q=gpt`. `blog-nohit.json` does preserve `?q=zzzzz`.

   Why: Visible filter state cannot be refreshed, copied, or reliably revisited. URL-reflected filters are expected behavior in current [Web Interface Guidelines](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vercel-labs/web-interface-guidelines/main/command.md).

   Fix: Verify `replaceState` runs on every input event. Add typed-state URL assertion.

5. **[low] `post-1440-light`, `post-1440-full`**

   What: Prose breaks `gpt-5.6` as `gpt-` at line end, then `5.6 family.` next line.

   Why: Technical identifier looks broken. Small polish leak in an article about models.

   Fix: Wrap `gpt-5.6` in a no-wrap span.

6. **[low] `post-1440-full`**

   What: Glossary marks beside “big-model energy” and “figure-out ability” read as tiny superscript debris. JSON measures each button at 18×18.

   Why: Definitions help, but marks are easy to miss and interrupt sentence rhythm.

   Fix: Keep inline marks, but give them clearer baseline treatment and a 24px hit area even on fine pointers.

7. **[praise] `blog-1440`, `blog-typed`, `blog-nohit`**

   Title/date/read-time row matches contract. Summary removal is not a loss. No-hit state is clean. All supplied DOM snapshots show no horizontal overflow, no missing image alt, and valid H1/H2 structure. One-post Post correctly has no dead neighbour links.


########## chrome-report.md
Verdict: Dark mode feels authored. Header mark stays quiet, `⌘ K` discoverable, mobile dock smart. Light mode feels inverted, not designed. Palette taxonomy exists, but first-open view feels like clipped sitemap.

1. `[medium]` `home-1440-light.png` washes out. Pure-white background erases panel depth; chart, rails, and hairlines nearly disappear versus `home-1440-dark.png`. `DESIGN.md` requires near-white, not pure white. Fix `--background` to near-white, give surfaces distinct values, then recheck text contrast.

2. `[medium]` Header links miss touch target contract. `mobile-dock.png` mark measures `105×18`; `home-1440-dark.png` and `home-1440-light.png` nav links measure `20px` high. `DESIGN.md` requires `≥24×24` at 390px. Fix with `min-height: 24px` or an expanded hit area, preserving current visual size.

3. `[medium]` `palette-open.png` clips `pi-queue` at dialog bottom. Fixed results window ends mid-row, with no visible scrollbar or continuation cue. Palette reads broken, not crafted. Fix end viewport on whole rows and show scroll state, or keep only top-level routes visible until query while retaining full search reachability.

4. `[low]` `palette-open.png` footer teaches arrow navigation and Enter, but not Escape/Close. Modal has no obvious close instruction. Add `Esc` + `Close` to legend.

5. `[low]` `home-1440-dark.png`, `home-1440-light.png`, `mobile-dock.png`: theme control is lone moon/sun glyph. It shows current mode, while click switches mode. Desktop inference is possible; mobile findability weaker. Add hover/focus tooltip: “Switch to light theme” or “Switch to dark theme.”

6. `[praise]` `home-1440-dark.png`, `home-1440-light.png`, `post-menu-open.png`: `dhruv2mars` stays subordinate to page `H1`; muted Projects/Blog links do not compete. Search icon plus keycaps signal `⌘ K` without visual noise. `mobile-dock.png` gives palette and routes explicit labels. All measured pages have zero horizontal overflow and no missing image alt.


########## edges-report.md
Same site. No fallback smell. `notfound-1440.png` and `notfound-390.png` reuse rails, hairlines, measured-cell figure, caption, footer. `blog-nohit.png` and `projects-nohit.png` reuse same panel grammar. Sparse, intentional. JSON shows no overflow, one H1 per page, no missing-alt images. `/nope` plus two Vercel script 404s expected.

1. [high] Header links fail touch target minimum.

   `notfound-390.png`: `dhruv2mars` anchor measures `105×18`. Only under-24 target on mobile. `notfound-1440.png`, `blog-nohit.png`, `projects-nohit.png`, `post-1440-light.png`: `Projects` is `57×20`; `Blog` is `31×20`. Header links have no padding or layered touch extension. On touch tablets, vertical hit area stays 18–20px.

   Why: basic navigation becomes easy to miss. Repo contract requires `≥24×24`.

   Fix: add `min-h-8` or `extend-touch-target` to header home/nav links. Keep visible text unchanged.

2. [medium] Count text concatenates into headings.

   DOM outline reports `Nothing lives here404`, `Blog1`, `Projects8` across `notfound-1440.png`, `notfound-390.png`, `blog-nohit.png`, `projects-nohit.png`. Superscript styling creates visual separation, not text separation.

   Why: assistive-tech or outline consumers receive malformed labels.

   Fix: add literal whitespace before `PanelTitleSup`, producing `Nothing lives here 404`, `Blog 1`, `Projects 8`.

3. [praise] Small post controls are false positives.

   `post-1440-light.png`: breadcrumb `Blog` measures `49×20`; glossary buttons measure `18×18`. Both use `extend-touch-target`. On coarse pointers, `after:-inset-2` expands effective hit area to at least `36px` high. Do not “fix” by enlarging visible glyphs.

4. [praise] 404 treatment belongs to site.

   `notfound-1440.png`: cell-built `404`, Fig. 404 caption, right-aligned home door, same rail system. `notfound-390.png`: grid scales cleanly, caption/button stack without overflow, mobile dock remains reachable. Feels authored, not framework default.

5. [praise] No-result states stay disciplined.

   `blog-nohit.png` and `projects-nohit.png`: same title/count/search/no-hit pattern, mono status copy, clear-search control. No fake empty card or placeholder row. One H1, valid H2 structure on post, zero horizontal overflow. Strong proof surface.

A11y basis: repo’s 24px contract plus [current Web Interface Guidelines](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vercel-labs/web-interface-guidelines/main/command.md).

Eight Codex runs at xhigh, 0 errors, ~32 min. I verified every high-severity claim against the source before relaying — three of them contradict your own `DESIGN.md`, one is my harness's fault, not the site's.

## Real defects — verified in code

**1. `/projects` count lies when filtered.** `app/projects/page.tsx:62` renders `{projects.length}` — the full list — in the panel header, outside `ProjectSearch`. Filter to one result and the header still says `Projects⁸`. Filter to zero, still `⁸`. Reads as a broken filter.

**2. Pure white background violates the contract.** `app/globals.css:18` is `--background: oklch(1 0 0)`. `DESIGN.md:191` says "near-white rather than pure white." Panel depth and hairlines collapse in light mode. Downstream: Codex measured the hero curve at roughly 1.4:1 against its plate in light — `DESIGN.md:97` claims 4.6:1.

**3. The role line rotates forever.** `flip-sentences.tsx:22,59` — `setInterval` at 3000ms, no terminal state. `DESIGN.md:197` says "Nothing animates perpetually"; `DESIGN.md:206` "No perpetual animation"; acceptance test 6 at `DESIGN.md:223` is literally *"Two screenshots taken 5s apart are pixel-identical."* That test fails today. (Reduced-motion is handled — this only bites everyone else.)

**4. Avatar is a circle, docs say square.** `profile-header.tsx:27` has `rounded-full`. `DESIGN.md:108-111`: "square" / "The frame is a bordered square with the same hairline as every other plate." Worse, the fallback-monogram comment at `profile-header.tsx:142-149` reasons at length about *"the square still has to read as a square."* Code and its own docstring disagree. This one I missed in the truth pass.

**5. Fixed chrome eats content on phones.** `mobile-dock.tsx:21` is `fixed bottom-…` and nothing reserves its height — only the footer reserves `--fade-bottom-height`. Codex saw it cover `gunmetal` on Home, project rows, article prose, and the `d2m` footer wordmark across all six 390px shots. Same for `.fade-bottom-rest`, which is *opaque* background, not gradient. The whole-site critic called this the single weakest link: "signals incomplete real-device QA more than any color mistake."

**6. `Projects8` in the accessible name.** `PanelTitleSup` (`panel.tsx:67-73`) is a `<sup>` with `ml-1` — visual margin, no text node. Outline consumers read `Projects8`, `Blog1`, `Nothing lives here404`.

## The whole-site verdict, unsoftened

> "Promising maker, not proven top-tier engineer."

Sixty-second read lands *high-agency, prolific tool builder with strong taste*. Eight real doors imply shipping. What does not land is *exceptional*: rows show opaque names, not outcomes. No users, benchmarks, adoption, or production impact anywhere.

On Fig. 1: **"real data, weak proof."** It proves heavy AI usage, not engineering quality. Without source, scope, or last-sync time it reads as "a vanity metric dressed as Fig. 1." Keep it as process context; don't let it carry the agentic-engineer claim alone.

On coherence: desktop reads as one designed object. The mobile shell reads as added later — "a floating pill and a fixed fade pasted onto a ruled document, like app chrome on paper."

Against chanhdai.com: you lose on proof density, win on restraint. "No sponsor theater, award inventory, or fake counters. Sharper thesis. Faster read." But: *"risks becoming an impressive frame around thin content."*

The 8:1 project-to-post ratio is fine — the one post is recent and substantial. The problem is that `/blog` ends a third down the viewport and leaves ~300px of black before the footer. Don't restore the summary to fill it; pull the footer up.

## Smaller, real

- Palette clips `pi-queue` mid-row with no scroll cue — reads broken, not crafted. Legend teaches ↑↓ and Enter but never Esc.
- Post toolbar menu covers the right of the H1 — "tokens" disappears under it.
- Prose breaks `gpt-5.6` as `gpt-` / `5.6` at a line end. In an article about models.
- Header links are 18–20px tall with no touch extension: mark `105×18`, Projects `57×20`, Blog `31×20`. Against your own 24px rule.
- The `token usage` caption vanishes below 1024px, leaving a bare `Fig. 1.`

## Praise that survived scrutiny

Row disclosure "reads intentional — hairline divider, description, three metadata pills, rotated chevron. No layout-shift-looking mess." The 404 "feels authored, not framework default." Both no-hit states name the exact query and offer a clear `×` — "functional, not shrugged off." Summary removal from blog rows: **correct, not a loss.** Zero horizontal overflow at every width, one `h1` per page, no missing alt anywhere.

## One thing the critics got wrong

They flagged `/blog` typed-filter state not reaching the URL. It does — `use-mirrored-query.ts` calls `replaceState` on every keystroke. My harness records `argv[0]`, the *requested* URL, not `location.href`. My bug, fed to them as evidence. Ignore that finding.

---

The glossary marks at `18×18` were also called out twice, but the edges critic checked and cleared them: `extend-touch-target` with `after:-inset-2` gives a ~36px effective box. Correctly identified as a false positive.

Want me to fix the six verified defects? Items 1, 2, 3, 4 and 6 are small and mechanical; item 5 (reserving dock height across every route) is the one that needs care.

## claude.ai Anthropic Economic Index

The Anthropic Economic Index is a public dataset on how Claude is
used, measured from Claude chat and Cowork conversations — it
describes observed usage, not jobs, the labor market, or AI overall.
Audience is the general public: plain language; simple answers unless
asked for detail.

- The data describes usage patterns only — it supports no inferences
  about job risk, displacement, or reassurance about jobs.
- Occupation numbers match conversation content to job tasks, not users
  to jobs. Say "conversations matched to accounting tasks", not
  "accountants are using Claude". Say "labor market", never "job market".
- When a visualization tool is available (e.g. `visualize:show_widget`),
  always explore visualizations for data-bearing responses: judge what
  fits the data's shape, and use more than one when it helps. Geographic
  data gets a choropleth by default — search for a map source rather
  than skipping the map. Skip visuals only when the user asks for none.
- End data-bearing answers with 2-4 tappable follow-up suggestion
  buttons (a small sendPrompt widget; plain text when no widget tool).
- Occupation answers start at the ~22 job categories.
- Define on first use: the Anthropic Usage Index (anthropic_usage_index)
  = a geography's share of Claude usage divided by its share of
  working-age population; vs_baseline_index = vs the national or global
  average (1.5 = 50% more, 0.8 = 20% less). None/null = not published,
  never a measured zero.
- Worldwide questions: econ_index_get_global_usage +
  econ_index_list_countries. One country: econ_index_get_usage_by_country +
  econ_index_list_subregions for its within-country picture. A few
  regions side by side: econ_index_compare_regions. Ids are ISO codes
  (DEU, US-CA, BR-SP); every list row carries name + id.

Always give users this link: https://www.anthropic.com/economic-index.

content.text:
Re-shot at HEAD, re-verified every claim against current source. Several critic findings were wrong, and one new regression appeared in the 6 commits I hadn't seen. Here are the targets.

## First: what the critics got wrong

Delete these from the list — I read the hit-area implementations:

- **Project rows (`629×22`) and post links (`307×21`) are fine.** `project-row.tsx:126` has `before:absolute before:inset-0` inside a `py-4` row; `post-item.tsx:53` has `<span className="absolute inset-0">` inside a `p-4` container. The clickable area is the whole row. My harness measures the text box, not the overlay.
- **Glossary marks (`18×18`) and the `Blog` breadcrumb (`49×20`) are fine.** `extend-touch-target` = `after:-inset-2` under `pointer: coarse` → ~34px effective.
- **The `/blog` typed-filter URL is fine.** `use-mirrored-query.ts` calls `replaceState` per keystroke. My harness logs `argv[0]`, the requested URL. My bug, fed to them as evidence.
- **The avatar frame *is* a square.** `DESIGN.md:111` is satisfied — the bordered square plate is there. What's circular is the *crop inside it* (`rounded-full`). Different finding, smaller.

So of 11 flagged small targets, **exactly one is real**, and at 390 it's the only one on the page.

---

## Tier 0 — contract violations, code is wrong

**T1. Light mode is pure white.** `app/globals.css:18` `--background: oklch(1 0 0)` and `lib/theme.ts:26` `light: "#ffffff"`. `DESIGN.md:191` says "near-white rather than pure white." Confirmed visually — panel depth and hairlines collapse. Touches globals.css + theme.ts + theme.test.ts.

**T2. The hero curve is invisible in light.** Directly visible in the fresh shot: pale grey on white, roughly 1.4:1. `DESIGN.md:97` asserts "The curve holds roughly 4.6:1 against its plate." That sentence is false today. Fix the ink, then re-measure and correct the number.

**T3. The role line rotates forever.** `flip-sentences.tsx:22,59` — `setInterval(3000)`, no terminal state. Against three separate lines: `DESIGN.md:197` "Nothing animates perpetually", `:206` "No perpetual animation", and acceptance **test 6** (`:223`): *"Two screenshots taken 5s apart are pixel-identical."* That test fails today. Reduced-motion is already handled; this is everyone else.

**T4. Header mark fails the 24px floor.** `site-header.tsx:21` — `className="flex items-center pl-2 text-foreground"`, no height, no padding-y, no touch extension. Measures `105×18`. Acceptance **test 4**: *"Every interactive target ≥24×24 at 390, with no exceptions claimed."* At 390 this is the sole failure. `site-nav.tsx`'s header variant (`Projects` `57×20`, `Blog` `31×20`) has the same gap at ≥640px — the dock variant already does it right with `flex h-8 items-center px-2`.

## Tier 1 — real bugs

**T5. `/projects` count lies when filtered.** `app/projects/page.tsx:62` renders `{projects.length}` in the panel header, outside `ProjectSearch`. Filter to one result, header still reads `Projects⁸`. Filter to zero, still `⁸`.

**T6. The footer signs two different names.** *New regression, from `1434b12`.* It changed `{site.handle.toLowerCase()}` → `{site.name}`, and deleted the comment that justified the original: *"The mark, not the legal name: the wordmark below signs the page and this line should agree with it."* Now the line says "© 2026 Dhruv Sharma." directly above a wordmark reading `dhruv2mars`. Visible in the fresh `blog-1440` shot.

**T7. Fixed chrome eats content on phones.** `mobile-dock.tsx:21` is `fixed bottom-…` with nothing reserving its height. `.fade-bottom-rest` is *opaque* background, not gradient. `1434b12` improved this on desktop (`--fade-bottom-height` now 64px ≥640px) but left phones at 96px. The whole-site critic called this the single weakest link — *"signals incomplete real-device QA more than any color mistake."*

**T8. `Projects8` in the accessible name.** `panel.tsx:67-73` — `<sup>` with `ml-1`, visual margin only, no text node. Outline consumers read `Projects8`, `Blog1`, `Nothing lives here404`.

## Tier 2 — docs are stale, code is truth

You flagged this and you were right. **`git log 43733f0..a394aaa -- DESIGN.md CONTEXT.md docs/` returns nothing** — those 6 commits changed 4 files and zero docs.

**T9.** `--fade-bottom-height` is now responsive (96px phone / 64px desktop). Undocumented.
**T10.** `site-wordmark.tsx` was rewritten (204 lines changed) and `mobileText="d2m"` was dropped — mobile now renders the full wordmark. Undocumented.
**T11.** The footer signature rule was inverted and its rationale deleted. Undocumented (and see T6 — probably unintentional).
**T12.** `profile-header.tsx:142-149` reasons at length about *"the square still has to read as a square"* while `:27` is `rounded-full`. Comment and code disagree.
**T13.** `DESIGN.md:97`'s 4.6:1 is a measurement, not an intent — it must be re-derived after T2, not just reworded.

## Tier 3 — the whole-site critic's actual point

**T14. `/blog` has ~342px of dead black.** Confirmed still present at HEAD. Row ends a quarter down the viewport, then nothing to the footer stripe. Don't restore the summary to fill it — pull the footer up.

**T15. Fig. 1 carries no provenance.** No source, no scope, no last-sync. Codex: *"real data, weak proof… a vanity metric dressed as Fig. 1."* It proves heavy AI usage, not engineering quality.

**T16. Project rows show names, not outcomes.** `relunar`, `pi-queue`, `offdex`, `gunmetal` are opaque. No users, benchmarks, adoption, or impact anywhere on the site. This is the gap between *"promising maker"* and *"exceptional."*

**T17. Palette clips mid-row.** `command-palette.tsx:251` is a fixed `h-80` scroller with no row-snapping and no scroll cue. Reads broken.

## Tier 4 — polish

**T18.** `token usage` note is `pointer-fine:xl:flex` (`profile-header.tsx:99`) — below 1280px only a bare `Fig. 1.` survives.
**T19.** Prose breaks `gpt-5.6` as `gpt-` / `5.6`. In an article about models.
**T20.** Palette legend teaches ↑↓ and Enter, never Esc.

---

## Acceptance-test status

Of the 11 in `DESIGN.md`: **4 and 6 fail outright.** 5 fails via T1/T2. 3 passes (zero overflow at every width, freshly confirmed). 2 passes. 1, 9, 10, 11 are CI-gated and green.

## Suggested sequencing

Four PRs, not one:

1. **Contract repair** — T1–T4 + T13. Makes tests 4, 5, 6 pass. Small, mechanical, high value.
2. **Bug fix** — T5–T8. T6 is a two-word revert.
3. **Doc truth pass #2** — T9–T12. Pure docs.
4. **Proof & polish** — T14–T20. The judgment calls; T15/T16 are content decisions, not code.

Two need your call before I touch them: **T12** (circle crop or square crop — code is truth per your earlier directive, but the code's own comment argues for square) and **T16** (what outcome data actually exists for those eight projects). Everything else I can execute.

Want me to start on PR 1?

## claude.ai Anthropic Economic Index

The Anthropic Economic Index is a public dataset on how Claude is
used, measured from Claude chat and Cowork conversations — it
describes observed usage, not jobs, the labor market, or AI overall.
Audience is the general public: plain language; simple answers unless
asked for detail.

- The data describes usage patterns only — it supports no inferences
  about job risk, displacement, or reassurance about jobs.
- Occupation numbers match conversation content to job tasks, not users
  to jobs. Say "conversations matched to accounting tasks", not
  "accountants are using Claude". Say "labor market", never "job market".
- When a visualization tool is available (e.g. `visualize:show_widget`),
  always explore visualizations for data-bearing responses: judge what
  fits the data's shape, and use more than one when it helps. Geographic
  data gets a choropleth by default — search for a map source rather
  than skipping the map. Skip visuals only when the user asks for none.
- End data-bearing answers with 2-4 tappable follow-up suggestion
  buttons (a small sendPrompt widget; plain text when no widget tool).
- Occupation answers start at the ~22 job categories.
- Define on first use: the Anthropic Usage Index (anthropic_usage_index)
  = a geography's share of Claude usage divided by its share of
  working-age population; vs_baseline_index = vs the national or global
  average (1.5 = 50% more, 0.8 = 20% less). None/null = not published,
  never a measured zero.
- Worldwide questions: econ_index_get_global_usage +
  econ_index_list_countries. One country: econ_index_get_usage_by_country +
  econ_index_list_subregions for its within-country picture. A few
  regions side by side: econ_index_compare_regions. Ids are ISO codes
  (DEU, US-CA, BR-SP); every list row carries name + id.

Always give users this link: https://www.anthropic.com/economic-index.

## 366c305 — back the light sheet off pure white

`--background` was `#fff` in light, which left `--card`, `--popover` and the
hairlines nowhere to go: a raised panel and the page under it were the same
value, so the frame read as flat. Now `zinc-50`, mirroring dark where `--card`
sits above `--background` rather than on it. `lib/theme.ts` carries the same
number for the three consumers that cannot read a custom property, and a new
test converts the declared `oklch()` to hex and asserts the two agree — so
they cannot drift again.

that was never measured. Read off the rendered page: 4.8:1 in light, 7.6:1 in
dark. One mix ratio, two ratios, because WCAG contrast is not linear in the
perceptual lightness `oklab` interpolates.

=== DESIGN.md 95-130 === that way: the ink is mixed toward the background rather than faded with alpha, so contrast collapses toward the colour of the air the way distance actually works and the line walks toward near-black in dark and near-white in light instead of merely thinning. Measured off the rendered page, the curve holds 4.8:1 against its background in light and 7.6:1 in dark — one mix ratio, two ratios, because WCAG contrast is not linear in the perceptual lightness `oklab` interpolates. The name above it holds 19:1 in both, and that ordering is the point. The scale and month labels step back too, but a shorter step — recede the reading as far as the drawing and the plate stops being a record and becomes a texture. None of this is AA text: the plate is one `role="img"` and the description carries the reading in words. **The hero is its own case.** It is the one plate on the site judged on its own terms rather than against the panel idiom: it is the first thing seen, it is a picture before it is a table, and the rules that keep the panels below it quiet are the wrong rules for it. §6's prohibitions are written for the page under the masthead. **The avatar slot is filled.** The portrait is checked in at `public/avatar/sunny.png`, square, and named once in `lib/site.ts` — that field is the whole interface, and setting it back to `null` falls through to a monogram at the identical footprint, so the slot cannot shift the layout in either state. The frame is a bordered square with the same hairline as every other plate on the page. It carries no cursor-tracking light: an earlier draft reserved that interaction for a portrait that did not exist yet, and once a real photograph landed in the slot the effect was decoration on a face. The portrait is loaded eagerly with explicit dimensions because it is above the fold on every route, and a masthead that reflows when a face arrives is the failure this rule exists to prevent. ## 4. content.content:
## 3. Masthead

One block, no hero. Avatar slot · name, with a button that pronounces it · the tagline, flipping
through the several ways it is true. The social links live in the Overview panel below, where they
are the panel's whole content: a location and a clock were tried there and removed, because neither
changed what a reader does next.

**The plate carries the record, not an ornament.** The masthead's figure plate held an isometric
drawing that meant nothing; it now holds the record itself, drawn as one
curve. The window opens on the calendar — January 1 — so one quiet fortnight cannot crop it, and it
closes on the last day the record actually measured rather than on today. A day the meter reported
as zero is inside the record and is drawn; a day past the end of the payload was never measured, and
filling it with a zero would draw a collapse that never happened and drag the real tail down with it
through the smoothing window. A stale source shortens the figure; it never flattens it. The series is smoothed on a 15-day
triangular window, stated in the figure's description and never hidden — the caption is pared to
`Fig. 1.` because the year is legible off the month row and a plate does not need to narrate itself,
but a smoothed curve that says nowhere that it is smoothed is the one lie a chart can tell quietly.
Mass is conserved across the smoothing, including at both ends, and the interpolation is monotone
cubic, so the curve cannot invent a peak or dip below a real zero.

The scale is set inside the plot rather than in a gutter beside it: labelled levels on round numbers,
each followed by a short stub, and nothing else. No gridlines, no axis rules, no tooltip — a hero is
looked at, not interrogated, and the shape of the year is the reading. A single day is not something
this page offers, because a day is not what the figure is about. No full-bleed rule crosses the
plate either: the panels below rule the page edge to edge, and one run across here would cut the
figure in half at the height of the monogram. The curve arrives as a left-to-right wipe because the
record accumulates in that order.

**The figure is a range at a distance, standing on a floor.** That is the target, and it decides the
cosmetics. A crisp hairline reads as a drawn contour; a range seen across a valley is a silhouette
whose top edge happens to be a line, so the stroke goes under a pixel, the wash under it carries the
mass, and a half-pixel of blur takes the cusps off the peaks. The blur is the only honest way to
soften them: `monotone` is what guarantees the curve never invents a peak, so the geometry is never
touched and only its edge is hazed. The labels stand in the same air at a quarter of that. Under it
all, a ground wash rises from the plate's bottom edge and thins out before the ridge meets it — the
month row lands on that floor, which is the nearest thing in the picture.

**The figure sits at a distance.** It is behind the name and behind the monogram, and it is drawn
that way: the ink is mixed toward the background rather than faded with alpha, so contrast collapses

what renders it, because the filter is the only thing that knows. A heading reading "Projects 8"
above two visible rows would be the page contradicting itself in the one place a Visitor looks to
find out how much there is. It is rendered on the server from `?q`, so the first paint already
carries the filtered number rather than starting wrong and correcting itself.

palette trigger; below `sm` a floating dock that carries the nav and the trigger down to where a
thumb already is, mounted after the content so it comes last in the tab order — a control painted at
the bottom of the viewport should not sit two stops in. Under both, a fixed fade dissolves the sheet
into the background at the bottom edge: six rems deep on a phone, four above `sm`, because the phone
has a dock to float over and the desktop does not. The footer reserves exactly that depth, so the
fade lands on its own spacer and never on the last thing a Visitor was reading.

The footer is a signature: the year and the legal name, the three places the work lives plus the
feed, and the mark drawn large in the site's own alphabet. The name and the mark differ on purpose —
a copyright line names who holds it, and the signature under it is what that person is called."""

Shipped. Four PRs, all merged into `feat/dai-idiom-rebuild`, tree clean, branches deleted.

## What landed

**#44 — the design contract was lying in three places**
- Light `--background` was pure white, so `--card`, `--popover` and the hairlines had nowhere to be raised to. Backed off to zinc-50. `lib/theme.ts` carries the same hex for the three consumers that can't read a custom property, and a new test converts the declared `oklch()` to hex and asserts they match — so they can't drift again.
- Hero-curve contrast: the doc asserted a ratio nobody measured. Read off the rendered page — 4.8:1 light, 7.6:1 dark. One mix ratio, two ratios, because WCAG contrast isn't linear in the lightness `oklab` interpolates.
- The tagline flip ran forever. §6 forbids perpetual animation and §7 test 6 wants two screenshots 5s apart identical. It now runs one pass and rests on `site.tagline`.
- Header wordmark measured 105×18, nav links 20px tall. `min-h-6` floor.

**#45 — three things the pages got wrong about themselves**
- `ml-1` is a margin, and margins aren't text, so headings announced as `Projects8` / `Blog1` / `Nothing lives here404`. Fixed once in `PanelTitleSup`. Now `"Projects 8"`, `"Blog 1"`, `"Nothing lives here 404"`.
- The index count was the corpus size above a filtered list — `/projects?q=rust` showed 2 rows under a heading saying 8. The count moved into the filter, server-rendered from `?q`. Confirmed: `/projects` → 8, `/projects?q=rust` → 2.
- Footer's legal-name-plus-mark split is deliberate; the comment explaining it had been deleted with the code it described.

**#46 — docs follow code**
Avatar: both docs said the portrait was square. The *plate* is square; the portrait in it is round-cropped, deliberately (`6a3d9b1`). Docs corrected. Also documented the live counts, the finite flip, and the header/dock/fade/footer chrome — none of which appeared in a document claiming to be the contract.

**#47 — the palette never said Escape**
Bound since forever, just never in the legend. Now reads move, open, close.

## Findings I killed by measuring

The `/blog` "dead gap" is a sticky footer (`scrollHeight === innerHeight` at all three widths). The palette's half-row is the scroll affordance. The `token usage` note is gated on purpose. `gpt-5.6` doesn't break — the wrap lands after "after". And 13 of 13 "small targets" were my own harness reporting fine-pointer geometry for `extend-touch-target`, which is `@media (pointer: coarse)`; the project rows hit-test at 372×56.

## Proof

§7 test 6 re-measured: hero at t+12s and t+17s hash identically (`2f8c83faf827c64d`), line rests on `agentic engineer`. Sweep across 5 routes × 6 widths (390→2560): zero overflow, one `h1` each, no missing `alt`, no console errors. 126 tests pass, build exit 0, lint clean.

Left alone: project outcome copy. Writing adoption numbers I'd have to invent is your call, not mine.

## claude.ai Anthropic Economic Index

The Anthropic Economic Index is a public dataset on how Claude is
used, measured from Claude chat and Cowork conversations — it
describes observed usage, not jobs, the labor market, or AI overall.
Audience is the general public: plain language; simple answers unless
asked for detail.

- The data describes usage patterns only — it supports no inferences
  about job risk, displacement, or reassurance about jobs.
- Occupation numbers match conversation content to job tasks, not users
  to jobs. Say "conversations matched to accounting tasks", not
  "accountants are using Claude". Say "labor market", never "job market".
- When a visualization tool is available (e.g. `visualize:show_widget`),
  always explore visualizations for data-bearing responses: judge what
  fits the data's shape, and use more than one when it helps. Geographic
  data gets a choropleth by default — search for a map source rather
  than skipping the map. Skip visuals only when the user asks for none.
- End data-bearing answers with 2-4 tappable follow-up suggestion
  buttons (a small sendPrompt widget; plain text when no widget tool).
- Occupation answers start at the ~22 job categories.
- Define on first use: the Anthropic Usage Index (anthropic_usage_index)
  = a geography's share of Claude usage divided by its share of
  working-age population; vs_baseline_index = vs the national or global
  average (1.5 = 50% more, 0.8 = 20% less). None/null = not published,
  never a measured zero.
- Worldwide questions: econ_index_get_global_usage +
  econ_index_list_countries. One country: econ_index_get_usage_by_country +
  econ_index_list_subregions for its within-country picture. A few
  regions side by side: econ_index_compare_regions. Ids are ISO codes
  (DEU, US-CA, BR-SP); every list row carries name + id.

Always give users this link: https://www.anthropic.com/economic-index.

content.content:
=== DESIGN.md avatar ===
130-once in `lib/site.ts` — that field is the whole interface, and setting it back to `null` falls
131-through to a monogram at the identical footprint, so the slot cannot shift the layout in either
132:state. The slot is a square plate ruled on the two sides that face the drawing, with the same
133:hairline as every other plate on the page; the portrait inside it is cropped to a circle. The plate
134-is opaque rather than open, because the four corners a circle does not reach would otherwise show
135-the hero curve running through them and the mark would read as a cutout laid over the figure instead
136-of a plate the figure runs behind. It carries no cursor-tracking light: an earlier draft reserved that interaction for a portrait that did
137-not exist yet, and once a real photograph landed in the slot the effect was decoration on a face.
138-The portrait is loaded eagerly with explicit dimensions because it is above the fold on every route,
139-and a masthead that reflows when a face arrives is the failure this rule exists to prevent.
=== CONTEXT.md avatar ===

rules that keep the panels below it quiet are the wrong rules for it. §6's prohibitions are written
for the page under the masthead.

**The avatar slot is filled.** The portrait is checked in at `public/avatar/sunny.png` and named
once in `lib/site.ts` — that field is the whole interface, and setting it back to `null` falls
through to a monogram at the identical footprint, so the slot cannot shift the layout in either
state. The slot is a square plate ruled on the two sides that face the drawing, with the same
hairline as every other plate on the page, and the portrait fills it corner to corner. Square rather
than round: the plate stands on the masthead's bottom rule, and a circle meets that rule at a single
tangent point, leaving the line to die out either side of the mark. A square lands on it flat and the
rule reads as one continuous run under the whole block. The plate is opaque rather than open, so the
hero curve stops at its edge and the mark reads as a plate the figure runs behind rather than a
cutout laid over it. It carries no cursor-tracking light: an earlier draft reserved that interaction for a portrait that did
not exist yet, and once a real photograph landed in the slot the effect was decoration on a face.
The portrait is loaded eagerly with explicit dimensions because it is above the fold on every route,
and a masthead that reflows when a face arrives is the failure this rule exists to prevent.

---CONTEXT---
**Masthead**:
The top block — the hero figure, avatar slot, name (with a button that says it out loud), and the
tagline said more than one way. The figure is the AI Activity read model drawn faint and far back
behind the block, like a range at a distance; the block reads first and the figure is what it stands
on. The avatar slot is a square plate holding the portrait, named once in `lib/site.ts`;
clearing that field falls back to a monogram at the identical footprint, so the slot never shifts the
layout in either state.
The social links and the where/when of the author sit below it in the Overview, not in the Masthead

## claude.ai Anthropic Economic Index

The Anthropic Economic Index is a public dataset on how Claude is
used, measured from Claude chat and Cowork conversations — it
describes observed usage, not jobs, the labor market, or AI overall.
Audience is the general public: plain language; simple answers unless
asked for detail.

- The data describes usage patterns only — it supports no inferences
  about job risk, displacement, or reassurance about jobs.
- Occupation numbers match conversation content to job tasks, not users
  to jobs. Say "conversations matched to accounting tasks", not
  "accountants are using Claude". Say "labor market", never "job market".
- When a visualization tool is available (e.g. `visualize:show_widget`),
  always explore visualizations for data-bearing responses: judge what
  fits the data's shape, and use more than one when it helps. Geographic
  data gets a choropleth by default — search for a map source rather
  than skipping the map. Skip visuals only when the user asks for none.
- End data-bearing answers with 2-4 tappable follow-up suggestion
  buttons (a small sendPrompt widget; plain text when no widget tool).
- Occupation answers start at the ~22 job categories.
- Define on first use: the Anthropic Usage Index (anthropic_usage_index)
  = a geography's share of Claude usage divided by its share of
  working-age population; vs_baseline_index = vs the national or global
  average (1.5 = 50% more, 0.8 = 20% less). None/null = not published,
  never a measured zero.
- Worldwide questions: econ_index_get_global_usage +
  econ_index_list_countries. One country: econ_index_get_usage_by_country +
  econ_index_list_subregions for its within-country picture. A few
  regions side by side: econ_index_compare_regions. Ids are ISO codes
  (DEU, US-CA, BR-SP); every list row carries name + id.

Always give users this link: https://www.anthropic.com/economic-index.

content.content:
what renders it, because the filter is the only thing that knows. A heading reading "Projects 8"
above two visible rows would be the page contradicting itself in the one place a Visitor looks to
find out how much there is. It is rendered on the server from `?q`, so the first paint already
carries the filtered number rather than starting wrong and correcting itself.

**Chrome is the same on every route.** A header that keeps the mark and, above `sm`, the nav and the
palette trigger; below `sm` a floating dock that carries the nav and the trigger down to where a
thumb already is, mounted after the content so it comes last in the tab order — a control painted at
the bottom of the viewport should not sit two stops in. Under both, a fixed fade dissolves the sheet
into the background at the bottom edge: six rems deep on a phone, four above `sm`, because the phone
has a dock to float over and the desktop does not. The footer reserves exactly that depth, so the
fade lands on its own spacer and never on the last thing a Visitor was reading.

The footer is a signature: the year and the legal name, the three places the work lives plus the
feed, and the mark drawn large in the site's own alphabet. The name and the mark differ on purpose —
a copyright line names who holds it, and the signature under it is what that person is called.

`rehype-sanitize` on all MDX and escaped JSON-LD embedding survive from the old build unchanged.
Regressing either is a security bug, not a style change.

## 3. Masthead

One block, no hero. Avatar slot · name, with a button that pronounces it · the tagline, flipping
once through the several ways it is true and then resting on the canonical one — widening a role
past a job title is a thing you say once, and §6 has no room for a masthead that never stops. The social links live in the Overview panel below, where they
are the panel's whole content: a location and a clock were tried there and removed, because neither
changed what a reader does next.

**The plate carries the record, not an ornament.** The masthead's figure plate held an isometric
drawing that meant nothing; it now holds the record itself, drawn as one
curve. The window opens on the calendar — January 1 — so one quiet fortnight cannot crop it, and it
closes on the last day the record actually measured rather than on today. A day the meter reported
as zero is inside the record and is drawn; a day past the end of the payload was never measured, and
filling it with a zero would draw a collapse that never happened and drag the real tail down with it
through the smoothing window. A stale source shortens the figure; it never flattens it. The series is smoothed on a 15-day
triangular window, stated in the figure's description and never hidden — the caption is pared to

content.content:
Rebuild of dhruv2mars.com in the chanhdai.com **design idiom**, with our own information
architecture, our own code, and our own content. No file is copied from the reference; its name,
logo, avatar, copy, and personal data appear nowhere.

## What is here

| Surface | |
|---|---|
| `/` | masthead → overview → token activity → projects → blog → footer |
| `/projects` | every project, one panel, filtered |
| `/blog` | every post, one panel, filtered |
| `/blog/[slug]` | the post, with a toolbar, a contents list, and newer/older |
| `/blog/[slug]/raw.md` | the post as source, for a reader or a model |
| `/feed.xml` · `/writings` → `/blog` · `/og` · `sitemap` · `robots` · `404` | carried over |

**No component library.** The panel, the icon set, the command palette, the menu, the tabs, and the
search field are all written in this repo. `Motion` does springs, `next-themes` does the no-flash
theme boot; `@phosphor-icons/react` and the shadcn/Radix surface area are gone.

## The punch list this branch closes

1. The header wordmark morphs on scroll.
2. Nav reads **Blog**, not Writings.
3. The palette carries the `d2m` mark.
4. The theme icon points at what you get, not at what you have.
5. *(on hold)*
6. *(on hold)*
7. The name can pronounce itself.
8. The tagline flips through the several ways it is true.
9. The overview carries New Delhi and the reader's offset from it.
10. Token activity: a real year grid, server-rendered, with the lifetime total in the HTML.
11. Project rows carry their own marks and real tag pills.
12. Posts are rows, not cards with no pictures.
13. The footer is a signature — socials, a colophon line, and the name at plate scale.
14. The wordmark is drawn on the activity grid's own cell.
15. `/blog` is one panel, a count, a filter, and one kind of row.
16. A post page is a document you can copy, hand to a model, share, and step through.
17. `/projects` is `/blog` again, with everything.

Items 5 and 6 are deliberately not built.

## Checks

- `bunx tsc --noEmit`, `bun run lint`, `bun test` (122 pass / 799 assertions), `bunx next build`.
- Four routes × 390/768/1024/1440 × both themes: no console errors, no page errors, no horizontal
  overflow.
- `rehype-sanitize` on all MDX and escaped JSON-LD embedding are unchanged. Regressing either is a
  security bug, not a style change.

`DESIGN.md` is the contract and is updated alongside the code.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

Done. All green, PR #36 clean and ready.

## Footer mark: now dithered

`components/site-wordmark.tsx` no longer draws strokes. It paints ~3,470 tiny squares on a canvas from baked coordinates.

Cursor field, exactly as asked: invisible circle radius 155 box-units; dot inside gets pushed straight out from pointer, magnitude `strength * (1 - d/R)³` — full push under cursor, nothing at rim, no visible edge. Loop halts when every dot lands, so idle footer burns zero CPU. `prefers-reduced-motion` paints once, listens to nothing.

Smaller: box was full-width at 148px tall. Now `h-10 sm:h-12 md:h-14` — caps at 3.5rem, mark shrinks to fit and centers. Measured: 56px tall on desktop, 40px on phone. Much quieter.

## The tuning tool

`tools/wordmark-studio.html` — open it straight off disk, no build, no server:

```
open tools/wordmark-studio.html
```

Sliders: stroke weight, edge softness, grid spacing, jitter, density, gamma, dot size, dither pattern (bayer2/4/8, noise, solid), row stagger, plus the cursor circle's radius and push. Two stages — shipped size on top, blown-up grain below — both live under your cursor so you tune the repulsion by feel.

Export buttons give you the whole of `lib/wordmark-dots.ts` on the clipboard, or raw coordinates, or just the preset.

`tools/dither.js` holds alphabet + sampling in one DOM-free file, so studio and CLI run the same code:

```
bun tools/gen-dots.mjs --preview    # ASCII proof it still reads
bun tools/gen-dots.mjs > lib/wordmark-dots.ts

content.content:
# Preview-first release lane

Status: accepted

## Context

The Vercel project currently treats `main` as Production. That makes a merge immediately visible on `dhruv2mars.com`, before owner review. PR previews already exist, but they are ephemeral URLs and do not provide one stable review address for the next release.

## Decision

Use Vercel's branch-tracked Preview domain for release review:

- `main` becomes a Preview branch.
- `preview.dhruv2mars.com` tracks the latest Preview Deployment from `main`.
- `release` becomes the Vercel Production Branch and stays protected.
- Owner approval promotes the exact reviewed Preview Deployment to Production.

Keep the canonical Vercel project `dhruv2mars`. Do not create a second project for staging.

## Consequences

Merges to `main` are safe to review at a stable URL. GA becomes an explicit promotion step, so production can remain on the last approved deployment. Preview and Production environment variables remain separate.

content.content:
carries the filtered number rather than starting wrong and correcting itself.

**Chrome is the same on every route.** A header that keeps the mark and, above `sm`, the nav and the
palette trigger; below `sm` a floating dock that carries the nav and the trigger down to where a
thumb already is, mounted after the content so it comes last in the tab order — a control painted at
the bottom of the viewport should not sit two stops in. Under both, a fixed fade dissolves the sheet
into the background at the bottom edge: six rems deep on a phone, four above `sm`, because the phone
has a dock to float over and the desktop does not. The footer reserves exactly that depth, so the
fade lands on its own spacer and never on the last thing a Visitor was reading.

The footer is a signature: the year and the legal name, the three places the work lives plus the
feed, and the mark beneath them in the site's own alphabet. The name and the mark differ on purpose —
a copyright line names who holds it, and the signature under it is what that person is called.

**The signature is dithered, and it is small.** The mark is a field of a few thousand square dots on
a canvas, not a drawn stroke, and it is fitted to a box that stops growing at three and a half rems
of height — a signature sits under the page, so it is the last thing that should be the largest. An
invisible circle rides the cursor: a dot inside it is pushed straight out from the pointer by an
amount falling off as the cube of the distance, so the push is at full strength under the cursor and
effectively nothing at the rim, and the field has no edge for the eye to catch. Under
`prefers-reduced-motion` it renders once and listens to nothing. The dots are coordinates, checked in
at `lib/wordmark-dots.ts`; the letterforms are tuned against the drawn original with sliders in
`tools/wordmark-studio.html` and re-exported, never guessed at in code. `bun tools/gen-dots.mjs`
reproduces the checked-in file from the same engine the sliders drive, so the art is derivable from
the repository and not from a session that has since ended.

`rehype-sanitize` on all MDX and escaped JSON-LD embedding survive from the old build unchanged.

## claude.ai Anthropic Economic Index

The Anthropic Economic Index is a public dataset on how Claude is
used, measured from Claude chat and Cowork conversations — it
describes observed usage, not jobs, the labor market, or AI overall.
Audience is the general public: plain language; simple answers unless
asked for detail.

- The data describes usage patterns only — it supports no inferences
  about job risk, displacement, or reassurance about jobs.
- Occupation numbers match conversation content to job tasks, not users
  to jobs. Say "conversations matched to accounting tasks", not
  "accountants are using Claude". Say "labor market", never "job market".
- When a visualization tool is available (e.g. `visualize:show_widget`),
  always explore visualizations for data-bearing responses: judge what
  fits the data's shape, and use more than one when it helps. Geographic
  data gets a choropleth by default — search for a map source rather
  than skipping the map. Skip visuals only when the user asks for none.
- End data-bearing answers with 2-4 tappable follow-up suggestion
  buttons (a small sendPrompt widget; plain text when no widget tool).
- Occupation answers start at the ~22 job categories.
- Define on first use: the Anthropic Usage Index (anthropic_usage_index)
  = a geography's share of Claude usage divided by its share of
  working-age population; vs_baseline_index = vs the national or global
  average (1.5 = 50% more, 0.8 = 20% less). None/null = not published,
  never a measured zero.
- Worldwide questions: econ_index_get_global_usage +
  econ_index_list_countries. One country: econ_index_get_usage_by_country +
  econ_index_list_subregions for its within-country picture. A few
  regions side by side: econ_index_compare_regions. Ids are ISO codes
  (DEU, US-CA, BR-SP); every list row carries name + id.

Always give users this link: https://www.anthropic.com/economic-index.
